In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surah al-Mu'min (Ghafir)

It is also called Surat al-Tawl, and it is Meccan.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "When I come upon the Ali Ha Mim (the Hawamim), I feel as though I am in gardens, and I take delight in them. The Hawamim are called the brocades of the Qur'an." And in some reports: "The likeness of the Hawamim in the Qur'an is like the striped garments among clothes."

Also in some reports, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever stands in prayer at night reciting the Hawamim, Allah will forgive him."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Ha Mim﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is an oath which Allah swore by. Qatadah said: it is one of the names of the Qur'an. Some have said: the Ha (ح) is from (al-Halim, the Forbearing), and the Mim (م) is from al-Malik (the King). Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Alif Lam Ra," "Ha Mim," and "Nun, wal-Qalam," taken together, are the name of al-Rahman. It is also said: "Ha Mim" means: Ha Mim, that which is to come to pass, i.e., He has decreed what is to come to pass. 'Isa ibn 'Umar recited "Ha Mim" with the Mim in the accusative, in the sense of "recite Hamim."

Al-Ashtar al-Nakha'i said in verse:

(It reminds me of Hamim while the spear is thrust... Why did Hamim not recite before the advance?)

And another poet, using ha-mim in the sense of "decreed," said:

(So my day has been decreed, and a people rejoice, as though there were no day for the mockers.)
"And His saying: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ — meaning: the Invincible in His dominion, the All-Knowing of His creation."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 3:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Forgiver of sin﴾, i.e., the Concealer of sin.

And His saying: ﴿Accepter of repentance﴾, i.e., of repentance.

And His saying: ﴿Severe in punishment﴾, i.e., severe in punishment against the disbelievers.

And His saying: ﴿Possessor of abundance﴾, i.e., of power. It was also said: of vastness and wealth. And it is said: it means favour (tafdil). Some of them said: Forgiver of sin to the one who says, "There is no god but Allah."

Hammad narrated from Thabit, who said: "I was in the tent of Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr, reciting this verse: ﴿Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of abundance﴾. A shaykh passed by on a white mule, and he said to me: 'Say: O Forgiver of sin, forgive me; O Accepter of repentance, accept my repentance; O Severe in punishment, pardon me; O Possessor of abundance, shade me with goodness.' Then I did not see the shaykh again."

And His saying: ﴿There is no god but Him; to Him is the final return﴾, i.e., the place of return.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 40, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of God﴾, meaning: none dispute concerning the signs of God by way of repudiating them through denial.

And His saying: ﴿except those who disbelieve﴾, meaning: those who deny them (jaḥada). And His saying: ﴿So let not their going to and fro through the lands deceive you﴾, meaning: their going to and fro through the lands in safety. Ibn Jurayj said: "Let not their trade from Mecca to Syria, and from Syria to Yemen, deceive you."

In some exegetical works it is related that the Companions of the Messenger of God said, in distress: "We are poor, while the disbelievers are wealthy and possess property," so God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse. According to this, the meaning of His saying: ﴿Let not their going to and fro through the lands deceive you﴾ is: let not their affluence and ample means deceive you.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 5:

His saying: ﴿Before them the people of Noah denied, and the factions after them⦘ — and they are those who conspired against the prophets.

And His saying: ﴿And every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him⦘ — meaning: to kill him. It is also said: to take him captive.

The Arabs call a captive "akhidh" (one seized), al-Azhari said: "to seize him so that they could gain power over killing him."

And His saying: ﴿And they disputed with falsehood⦘ — meaning: with false disputation, so that by it they might refute the truth. Al-jidal (disputation) is turning the opponent away from what he holds, whether in truth or in falsehood. As for munazara (debate), it occurs only between those who are both upholders of the truth, or between one upholder of the truth and one who is in error. Jidal, however, may occur between those who are both in error.

And His saying: ﴿Then I seized them⦘ — meaning: I seized them with punishment.

And His saying: ﴿So how was My punishment?⦘ Qatadah said: "Severe, by God."

Almost-literal translation of the passage:

Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿Thus has the word of your Lord been justified against those who disbelieved﴾ meaning: the decree of your Lord has become binding upon those who disbelieved, that they are ﴿companions of the Fire﴾. The meaning is apparent.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 7:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it﴾. Al-Naqqash mentioned that the bearers of the Throne are the Karubiyyun (the cherubim), and they are the masters of the angels. In some tafsir works it is said that their feet are in the lowest parts of the earths, while the earths and the heavens reach to their waists, and they say: "Glory be to the Lord of might and dominion! Glory be to the Lord of sovereignty and majesty! Glory be to the Living who does not die! Most Holy, Most Pure, Lord of the angels and the Spirit."

And His words, ﴿and those around it﴾, meaning: around the Throne.

And His words, ﴿glorify their Lord with praise﴾, have already been explained.

And His words, ﴿and they seek forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge"﴾, meaning: Your knowledge encompasses [and] Your mercy encompasses all things.

And His words, ﴿so forgive those who repent and follow Your way﴾, meaning: Your religion and Your obedience.

And His words, ﴿and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, meaning: and ward off from them the punishment of the Blazing Fire. Al-Jahim is the greatest part of the Fire. It is related from some of the early scholars: the most sincere of creation toward the believers are the angels, and the most deceitful of creation toward the believers are the devils.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 8:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them﴾. We have explained that the Garden of Eden (jannat ʿadn) is the innermost part of the Garden (baṭnān al-jannah). It is also said: Egypt is the Garden.

His words: ﴿and whoever was righteous among their forefathers﴾, meaning: whoever affirmed the Oneness (of God) among their forefathers. It is also said: whoever did righteous deeds among their forefathers.

His words: ﴿and their spouses and their offspring﴾, meaning: their wives and their children. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: The believer enters the Garden and says: "Where is my father? Where is my mother? Where is my wife?" It is said to him: "They did not do deeds like yours." He says: "I did deeds for myself and for them." So God admits them into the Garden and gathers them to him.

And it is reported from some of the early generations (al-salaf) that he said: The believer loves to have his family gathered together and joined to him, so God gathers his family and joins them to him in the Hereafter.

And His saying: ﴿And protect them from the evil deeds﴾ — we have already explained it.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever is protected from the evil deeds that Day﴾ means: whoever is protected from the evil deeds that Day, i.e., the punishments; and it is said: the recompense of the evil deeds.

And His saying: ﴿then You have indeed had mercy on him﴾ means: You have bestowed favor upon him.

And His saying: ﴿And that is the great triumph﴾ means: the great salvation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 10:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to﴾. In the explanation: the disbeliever will be confronted with his evil deeds, so he will loathe himself with the utmost loathing. Then Allah the Most High will call out to them: {The loathing of Allah is greater than your loathing of yourselves}, meaning: Allah's loathing of you in the world is greater than your loathing of yourselves today, because of the evil deeds of yours that have become apparent to you. The meaning of this has been related from Ibn 'Abbas. Some of them said: Allah's loathing of you in the world is greater than the loathing some of you have for one another, and that is when they disown one another.

His words: ﴿when you were called to the faith but you disbelieved﴾, meaning: Allah's loathing of you was because Allah called you to the faith and you disbelieved.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, You made us die twice and gave us life twice."﴾ The first death is that they were drops of semen in the loins of their fathers, dead. Then He gave them life by creating them and breathing the spirit into them. Then He causes them to die the known death, which everyone must taste. Then He gives them life on the Day of Resurrection. This is the view of Mujahid, Qatadah and a group of others.

The second view concerning the verse is that the first giving of life was when He brought them out from the loins of Adam and took the covenant from them. Then He caused them to die by returning them to the loins, then gave them life by bringing them out a second time, then He causes them to die the known death. If it is said: "Where is the life in the Hereafter?" we say: what is meant according to this view is two lives and two deaths in this world, besides the life in the Hereafter.

The third view: the first death is the known death, the first giving of life is the life in the grave for questioning, the second death is the death after the life in the grave, and the second giving of life is the life for resurrection. This is what al-Suddi mentioned.

His saying: ﴿So we have acknowledged our sins﴾, i.e., our wrongdoings.

His saying: ﴿Is there any way to get out?﴾, i.e., is there any way out of the Fire?

That is, your eternal abiding in the Fire and your remaining in it was because when Allah alone was called upon, you disbelieved.

﴿And if partners were associated with Him, you believed﴾: meaning, if partners were associated with Allah, you would believe, i.e., you would affirm polytheism.

As for His saying, ﴿So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great﴾, its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 13:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs﴾, meaning: His lessons (ʿibar) and proofs (dalāʾil).

And His saying: ﴿and sends down for you provision from the sky﴾, meaning: the rain, because it is the cause of sustenance (arzāq).

And His saying: ﴿And none remembers except those who turn back (in repentance)﴾, meaning: none takes heed except those who return to God in all their affairs.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾, i.e., sincere to Him in monotheism (al-tawhid). Its meaning: declare Allah one and do not associate anything with Him.

And His saying: ﴿although the disbelievers dislike it﴾, i.e., the disbelievers become angry, and this is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That He may cause it to prevail over all religion, although the polytheists dislike it﴾. We have already explained this earlier.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 15:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Raised in degrees, Lord of the Throne﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said, by the transmission of 'Ata': "Raiser of the heavens, one heaven above another." And it is related from some of them: "Raiser of the degrees of the prophets and the friends of God (awliya')." Others said: "Raised in degrees" means "great in attributes," and this refers back to God the Exalted; so said Muqatil. He said: "God is above everything, and there is nothing above Him."

And His saying: ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾, meaning: the Throne belongs to Him, in creation and in dominion.

And His saying: ﴿He sends down the Spirit by His command﴾. Mujahid said: it is the revelation (wahy), and it was called a spirit because creatures are given life by it. Qatadah said: it is prophethood (nubuwwah). It has also been said: it is Gabriel, whom He sends upon whomever of His prophets He wills. And the spirit of a human being is that by which a human being is alive.

And His saying: ﴿by His command﴾, meaning: by His order.

And His saying: ﴿upon whomever of His servants He wills﴾, from among the prophets and messengers.

And His saying: ﴿that he may warn of the Day of Meeting﴾. The well-known reading is with the yā' (ya), and it has been read with the tā' (ta).

With the yā', meaning: that God may warn; it has also been said: that the revelation may warn. As for the reading with the tā', the intended meaning is the Messenger.

And His saying: ﴿the Day of Meeting﴾. Qatadah said: on it the inhabitants of heaven and the inhabitants of earth meet, the first and the last. And it is related from some of them: on it the creature and the Creator meet. Maymun ibn Mihran said: on it the oppressor and the oppressed meet. And it is related from Ibn 'Abbas: on it Adam and the last of his offspring meet.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 16:

And His saying: ﴿The Day they will emerge,﴾ meaning: they will be exposed and manifest, with nothing to conceal them behind a mountain or anything else.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Nothing of them will be hidden from Allah.﴾ Meaning: of their deeds.

And His saying: ﴿"Whose is the sovereignty today?"﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah the Exalted says this when creation has perished, and there is no one left to answer Him, so He answers Himself, saying: ﴿"To Allah, the One, the Subduer."﴾ This is the view of the majority of the commentators. It has been established, through the narration of Ibn 'Umar and others, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah will seize the heavens and the earth in His right hand, then shake them and say: 'I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?'"

There is another view regarding the verse: that Allah the Exalted will raise up the creatures and gather them, then say to them: ﴿"Whose is the sovereignty today?"﴾ and they will answer: "To Allah, the One [and] the Subduer."

It has also been said: they will be unable to answer out of awe, so Allah the Exalted will answer Himself. The first view is the best known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned﴾, meaning: the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil.

His saying: ﴿There is no injustice today﴾, meaning: that He, may He be exalted, does what He does with justice, not with injustice.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. In the exegesis: Allah, may He be exalted, will reckon with them within the span of half a day of the days of this world. And it is related from al-Dahhak: the span between two prayers. It has also been said: the span of a sip of water.

It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The first matter Allah, may He be exalted, will judge among the creation concerns blood."

And in some reports: Allah, may He be exalted, says on the Day of Resurrection: "I am the King, the Judge. No one among the people of Paradise shall enter Paradise while he has a wrong against anyone among the people of the Fire, nor shall anyone among the people of the Fire enter the Fire while he has a wrong against anyone among the people of Paradise, unless I exact retribution for it from him."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 18:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And warn them of the Approaching Day﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection. It was called al-Azifa (the Approaching) because of its nearness, as if it were near to God the Most High, even though people deem it far off. It was also said: it is near because it is certainly going to happen, and everything that is certain to occur is near.

His words: ﴿When the hearts will be at the throats⁠—﴾ It is related from ʿIkrima that he said: The earth of the Resurrection will become constricted for people, until no one has anything but the place of his foot. Then it will constrict for them further, until foot is placed upon foot. Then they will weep until their tears are exhausted, then they will weep blood until it is exhausted. Then their hearts will rise up to their throats. Then he recited the words of the Most High: {And warn them of the Approaching Day, when the hearts will be at the throats, [choking]}. Qatada said: The hearts will rise from the chests to the throats, cleaving to them from fear and terror, so they neither return to their places nor come out.

His words: ﴿choking﴾. Al-kazim is the one who holds his heart in check over what is in it. It was also said: distressed and grieved. It is also said: weeping. From this comes kazm al-ghayz (swallowing anger), when one holds it in and (endures) it.

His words: ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend, nor any intercessor who would be obeyed⁠—﴾ The ḥamīm is the close friend. The shafīʿ is the one who supplicates and is answered. It is related from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī that he said: Multiply your friendships with the believers, for they have intercession with God the Most High.

His words: ﴿who would be obeyed﴾, meaning: who would be answered.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 40, verse 19:

And His saying: {He knows the treachery of the eyes}. That is: the treachery of the eyes, and the treachery of the eyes is the hasty glance at what is not lawful.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the man who is among men, and a woman passes by them, so he looks at her; and when his companions notice him, he lowers his gaze.

Al-Suddi said: "The treachery of the eyes is the winking with the eye."

And His saying: ﴿And what the breasts conceal﴾ is the desire of the heart. It was also said: it is that, if he were able to do it, would he commit adultery or not?

And on the authority of al-Suddi, he said: it is the whispering of the heart. And on the authority of some of them, he said: "The treachery of the eye" is that he says, "I saw," when he did not see; and the treachery of the heart is that he says, "I knew," when he did not know.

His saying: ﴿And Allah judges with truth﴾, i.e., with justice.

His saying: ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him﴾, i.e., the idols and whatever is similar to them.

His saying: ﴿do not judge anything﴾, i.e., they do not decide anything, because they have no power over anything whatsoever.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Almighty God's saying: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces left upon the earth.﴾ "Traces upon the earth" refers to the buildings, dwellings, and all the other structures.

And His saying: ﴿So God seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against God.﴾ That is: there was no one to shield them from God.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs﴾, i.e., with evidences and miracles.

And His saying: ﴿So they disbelieved, and God seized them. Indeed, He is Strong, severe in punishment﴾. Its meaning is apparent.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority﴾. That is, with the manifest miracles and the evident proof.

The Qur'anic quotation: ﴿To Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun, and they said: "A sorcerer, a liar."﴾ That is, "kadhdhab" means one who lies much (kathir al-kadhib). It is reported from al-Dahhak that he said: Haman was not from the Children of Israel, nor from the Copts, and he was from neither of the two groups. Some have criticized this, saying: Haman is a well-known man among the Persians, and he was not the companion of Pharaoh. This is not a valid objection, because it is possible that there was a man among the Persians called Haman, and the companion of Pharaoh was (also) Haman, so everything in the Qur'an is true and correct.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, "Kill the sons of those who believe with him."﴾ In the story: Pharaoh had lifted the killing from the sons of the Children of Israel; then, when Musa came to him as a messenger, he reinstated the killing against them.

And His saying: ﴿And spare their women.﴾ We have already explained it.

And His saying: ﴿And the plotting of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾ That is, in destruction. He made their plotting destruction only because it leads to their destruction.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 26:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "Leave me to kill Moses."﴾ If someone says: Who was it that was preventing Pharaoh from killing Moses, such that he would say, "Leave me to kill Moses"? The answer has two aspects. The first: its meaning is, "Leave me to kill Moses," that is, "Advise me concerning the killing of Moses," as if he sought their counsel: should he kill him or not kill him?

The second: among his people there were some who warned him against killing Moses, fearing the destruction of Pharaoh. So he said, on this basis: "Leave me," do not prevent me, and leave me to kill him.

His words: ﴿And let him call upon his Lord﴾ mean: and let him call upon his Lord so that He may help him. He said this by way of disbelief (istib'ad).

His words: ﴿Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion﴾ mean: that he will change your religion, which you are upon, into something else.

His words: ﴿Or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land﴾ this has four readings: "an yuzhira" and "an yuzhira" without the alif; "aw an yuzhiraa" with the alif and the yā' in the accusative; and "wa an yuzhira" without the alif and the yā' in the accusative. The meaning of yuzhira (is that) Moses makes corruption appear; and the meaning of yuzhira with a fatḥa on the yā' is that corruption itself appears, as if he made the verb belong to corruption itself. Some of them said: the meaning of corruption here is that when Moses prevails, he will kill your sons and spare your women, just as you have done to them; so this is Moses making corruption appear in the land.

Almost-literal translation follows.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Moses said, "Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning."﴾

The people of tafsir (ahl al-tafsir) said: When Moses heard the words of Pharaoh, he sought refuge in Allah and turned to Him, saying: "Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord."

As for His words ﴿from every arrogant one﴾, that means: from every one who magnifies himself (mutakabbir, one who regards himself as great). ﴿who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning﴾: the Day of Reckoning (yawm al-hisab) is the Day of Resurrection (yawm al-qiyamah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh said﴾. Al-Kalbi said: He was among those who were heirs to the succession (wali al-'ahd) of Pharaoh, and the kingship would pass to him after Pharaoh. It is also said that he was a paternal cousin of Pharaoh. And it is reported from some of them that he was from the Children of Israel. According to this view, there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse, so its meaning is: "And a man who concealed his faith from the family of Pharaoh said."

As for his name, some said: his name was Hizbil. In the Ma'ani of al-Zajjaj, it is stated that his name was Sam'an. It was also said: Habib. In the tafsir literature it is mentioned that no one from the Copts believed except three men: the wife of Pharaoh, the believer from the family of Pharaoh, and the man who came and said, "O Musa, the chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you."

His saying: ﴿Will you kill a man because he says, "My Lord is Allah"?﴾ That is: because he says, "My Lord is Allah."

His saying: ﴿And he has certainly brought you clear proofs from your Lord﴾ That is: with clear evidences.

His saying: ﴿And if he is a liar, upon him is his lie﴾ That is: upon him is the harm of his lie.

His saying: ﴿And if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you﴾ This is a problematic verse, because he said: ﴿some of what he promises you﴾, whereas everything the messengers and Musa promised is true. The answer to this is in several respects:

First: the meaning of his saying ﴿some of what he promises you will befall you﴾ is "all of what he promises you," so "some" is used in the sense of "all." This was stated by Abu 'Ubayda, who recited:

(Or some souls' doves are bound...)

That is, all souls.

And another recited:

(The hasty one may attain some of his need, and the patient one may attain some of his need, and with the hasty one there is often error...)

His saying "some of his need" means all of his need.

The second aspect: he said ﴿some of what he promises you﴾ by way of emphasis (istizhar), as if he said: at the least, if you deny him and he is truthful, some of what he promises you will befall you, and in that "some" is your destruction. The grammarians hold that this is better than the first view, because "some" meaning "all" is not known in the language.

The third aspect: his saying ﴿some of what he promises you will befall you﴾ means the punishment of this world, and they had been promised the punishment of this world and of the Hereafter.

The fourth aspect: his saying ﴿some of what he promises you will befall you﴾ means some of the punishment, since he had promised punishment if they denied and reward if they believed, and punishment is part of the threat.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor, a liar﴾ That is: a polytheist, a liar.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 29:

The Most High's saying: ﴿O my people, yours is the dominion today, dominant in the land﴾ means: exalted and victorious.

And His saying: ﴿So who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes upon us?﴾ means: who will prevent from us the punishment of Allah if it comes upon us.

And His saying: ﴿Pharaoh said, "I show you only what I see"﴾ means: I guide you only to what I myself follow, and I show you only the truth that I see.

And His saying: ﴿and I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾ means: the way of right guidance and direction. It is narrated from Mu'adh ibn Jabal that he recited, "إِلَّا سَبِيل الرشاد" with the letter shin doubled, meaning: the path of Allah, and "al-rashad" is Allah the Most High.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the one who believed said, "O my people, I fear for you a day like the day of the factions."﴾

"The factions" (al-Ahzab): the former nations, such as the people of Nuh (Noah), 'Ad, and Thamud.

The meaning of "the day of the factions" is: the day of their punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 31:

And His saying: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Noah, and ʿAd, and Thamud﴾. Al-daʾb (custom, habit) in the language means habit, and the meaning of His saying: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Noah﴾ is: like the condition of the people of Noah, and ʿAd, and Thamud. It is said: these people denied, and they accustomed themselves to denial, like the habit of those in denying.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah does not intend injustice for the servants﴾ means: He does not punish anyone until He establishes the proof against him.

"And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Tanād (mutual calling out)."

That is: the Day of Tanādī (the Day of Mutual Calling). There are several meanings of tanādī:

The first: each community is called out with its book and its leader. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: the meaning is that the people of Paradise call out to the people of the Fire, and the people of the Fire call out to the people of Paradise. This is mentioned in Surah al-A'raf, in His saying, ﴿And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, "We have found true what our Lord promised us"﴾ and so on, and His saying: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise﴾ and so on.

The third: the meaning of the verse is their calling out with "Woe" and "Destruction," and their supplicating against themselves: "Alas my ruin!", "Alas my woe!", and other such cries. It is also recited in the non-canonical reading as "yawm al-tanādd" (with a doubled dāl), from nadda yanuddu, meaning to flee; this reading is transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Where is the escape?﴾. And it is reported from some of them: a neck will appear from the Fire, and the people will flee, but that neck will encircle them. At that point they will know that there is no escape for them.

The Qur'anic verse "﴿يَوْم تولون مُدبرين﴾" is translated by al-Sam'ani as follows.

And His saying: ﴿On the Day you turn your backs fleeing﴾. In a hadith it is said that people will have a turning-away (jawla) on the Day of Resurrection, and the angels will follow them and turn them back. It was also said: when they hear the roaring (zafir) of the Fire, they flee, and this is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On the Day you turn your backs fleeing﴾. There is another view concerning the verse: that the meaning of His saying ﴿On the Day you turn your backs fleeing﴾ is their being driven to the Fire by the angels' driving.

And His saying: ﴿You will have no protector from Allah﴾. That is, no preventer (māni'); and it was said: no helper (nāṣir).

And His saying: ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾. Its meaning is evident.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Joseph came to you before with clear proofs﴾, refers to Joseph son of Jacob, the Prophet of God. It is related from some scholars that God sent to them, meaning to the Copts, a prophet from the jinn named Joseph. This is a weak opinion, and the sound one is the first, because the mention of Joseph is unqualified, so it refers to the well-known Joseph, just as (it refers to) Abraham, Moses, Jesus and others. In the narrative: God sent Joseph son of Jacob to them as a messenger, and he called them to God, and he remained among them twenty years after the death of Jacob, peace be upon him.

His saying: ﴿with clear proofs﴾, meaning: with evident signs.

His saying: ﴿So you continued in doubt about what he brought you, until when he died you said, "God will never send after him a messenger."﴾ Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud read: "Alan yab'athu Allahu min ba'dihi rasulan" (أَلَن يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ رَسُولًا), with an added alif.

His saying: ﴿Thus God leaves astray whoever is a transgressor, a doubter.﴾ Meaning: one who is excessive against himself through disbelief and wrongdoing, and "the doubter" is the skeptic.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 35:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them﴾. The meaning of al-mujadala (disputation) here is disputing by denying (al-takdhib), and the meaning of sultan (authority) is proof (al-hujja).

And His words: ﴿Greatly hateful it is in the sight of Allah and of those who believe﴾. That is: their disputation is greatly hateful. In the tafsir it is said that Allah hates them, and the angels and prophets hate them, and the believers hate them, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿in the sight of Allah and of those who believe﴾.

And His words: ﴿Thus does Allah seal upon every heart of an arrogant tyrant﴾. The first reading is in the idafa (construct form), and tab' (sealing) upon the heart is the khatm (stamping) upon it so that the truth does not enter it.

As for the second reading, it is on describing the heart as arrogant, as one says: "a proud heart" (qalb mutakabbir), meaning its owner is arrogant. Ibn Mas'ud read: "upon the heart of every arrogant tyrant."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verses 36–37:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O Haman..."﴾ Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Haman was the chief of police (sahib shurta) of Pharaoh, and he was from Hamadan. Abu al-Hasan ibn Faris transmitted this in his tafsir.

And His saying: ﴿Build for me a tower﴾, meaning: a lofty palace. It is said: the first person to bake bricks until they became fired brick (ajurr) was Haman, and he did this for Pharaoh. In the tafsir of al-Naqqash it is reported that Haman employed fifty thousand people in the construction, apart from those who baked the bricks and those who worked in wood and other materials.

It is also said that he worked on the building of the tower for seven years, and Pharaoh would ascend it riding. Then Allah the Exalted sent a violent wind which broke it into three pieces: one piece He cast into the sea, one piece into India, and one piece into the lands of the West.

And His saying: ﴿So that I may reach the means, the means to the heavens﴾. Here "asbab" (means, ways) signifies "abwab" (doors). It is also said that its meaning is: the means that will lead me to the sky and bring me to it. If it is asked: how can it be conceived in the mind of any sane person that he intended to ascend to the sky, when that is impossible by such a stratagem?

The answer: ignorance in the world is abundant, and this is no more extraordinary than his claim to lordship, while he knows his own condition and observes it.

And His saying: ﴿And I surely think him a liar﴾ regarding his claim that Moses has a god.

And His saying: ﴿Thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed﴾, meaning: his ugly deed.

And His saying: ﴿and he was barred from the way﴾. It is also read "wa-saddu" with the sad vowelled with a fatha. The reading with the damma means: Pharaoh barred himself from the way. With the fatha it means: Pharaoh barred the people from the way of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin﴾, meaning: the stratagem and deceit of Pharaoh resulted only in destruction and loss, and He said this because it led to that.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verses 36–37:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O Haman..."﴾ Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Haman was the chief of police (sahib shurta) of Pharaoh, and he was from Hamadan. Abu al-Hasan ibn Faris transmitted this in his tafsir.

And His saying: ﴿Build for me a tower﴾, meaning: a lofty palace. It is said: the first person to bake bricks until they became fired brick (ajurr) was Haman, and he did this for Pharaoh. And His saying: ﴿And I surely think him a liar﴾ regarding his claim that Moses has a god.

And His saying: ﴿Thus was made attractive to Pharaoh the evil of his deed﴾, meaning: his ugly deed.

And His saying: ﴿and he was barred from the way﴾. It is also read "wa-saddu" with the sad vowelled with a fatha. The reading with the damma means: Pharaoh barred himself from the way. With the fatha it means: Pharaoh barred the people from the way of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿And the plot of Pharaoh was not but in ruin﴾, meaning: the stratagem and deceit of Pharaoh resulted only in destruction and loss, and He said this because it led to that.
The words of the Most High: ﴿And the one who believed said, "O my people, follow me, and I will guide you to the path of right guidance."﴾ Meaning: the path of *rushd* (right guidance and rectitude).

"And His saying: ﴿O my people, this worldly life is only a passing enjoyment﴾, meaning: its passing away is swift, and enjoying it is brief.

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the abode of permanence﴾, meaning: the place of settling."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 40:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like; and whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer – those will enter Paradise, where they will be provided for without reckoning.﴾ That is: without cessation. It is also said: "without reckoning" means that their period of stay in Paradise and their enjoyment are not counted against them, so that it is said: their stay is such-and-such, their eating is such-and-such, their deeds are such-and-such. And it is said: "without reckoning" means that He increases the duration of their remaining in Paradise over the duration of their deeds to a period without end.

Almighty ways of Allah's speech: "And, O my people, what is with me that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire? You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, while I call you to the All-Mighty, the Oft-Forgiving."

Al-'Aziz (the All-Mighty) is the One who takes vengeance on His enemies, and al-Ghaffar (the Oft-Forgiving) is the One who covers the sins of His servants.

Almighty ways of Allah's speech: "And, O my people, what is with me that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire? You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, while I call you to the All-Mighty, the Oft-Forgiving."

Al-'Aziz (the All-Mighty) is the One who takes vengeance on His enemies, and al-Ghaffar (the Oft-Forgiving) is the One who covers the sins of His servants.

La jarama (lā jarm) — as explained earlier, its meaning has already been clarified. It is reported from al-Mufaddal al-Dabbi al-Kufi that he said: "lā jarm" means "lā budda" (there is no doubt, it is certain).

As for His saying: ﴿There is no call to him in this world nor in the Hereafter﴾ — that is, no answering of a call in this world. It is also said: it means bringing benefit in this world nor in the Hereafter. It is also said: the answer to His saying ﴿nor in the Hereafter﴾ is ﴿there is no call to him in this world nor in the Hereafter﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿And that our return is to Allah﴾ — that is, our return is to Allah.

As for His saying: ﴿And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾ — that is, the polytheists.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So you will remember what I am telling you﴾, meaning: when you witness the punishment.

And His saying: ﴿And I entrust my affair to Allah﴾, meaning: I surrender my affair to Allah. Yahya ibn Sallam said: meaning, I put my trust in Allah.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 45:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So Allah saved him from the evil of what they schemed﴾. Scholars differed concerning his deliverance. Some said: he was saved when Moses and the Children of Israel were saved, and that was at the crossing of the sea. In the narration: he was in front of Moses when they set out toward the sea, and he said, "Where to, O Prophet of Allah?"

He said, "Ahead of you."

He said, "Rather, ahead of me is the sea."

Then he said, "By Allah, I have not lied, nor have I been lied to."

The second view: when the believer from the family of Pharaoh made these statements and gave this advice, Pharaoh sought to kill him, so he fled. Pharaoh sent a group in pursuit, and they found him in a mountain pass, praying, with wild beasts around him guarding him, so they were terrified and turned back.

And his saying: ﴿And there befell the family of Pharaoh the worst of punishment﴾, meaning: there descended upon the family of Pharaoh, ﴿the evil punishment﴾, meaning: the wretched punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 46:

The words of the Most High: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾. Most of the commentators hold that this refers to the grave. It is well known from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "The spirits of the family of Pharaoh are in the crops of black birds; they are brought to the Fire morning and evening." It is also firmly established, through the narration of Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When any one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening: if he is among the people of Paradise, then (it is) Paradise; and if he is among the people of the Fire, then (it is) the Fire. It is said: 'This is your seat until the Day of Resurrection.'" He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: We were informed of this by al-Makki ibn 'Abd al-Razzaq al-Kashmihayni, who said: we were informed by Abu al-Haytham, my grandfather, who said: we were informed by al-Firabri, who said: we were informed by al-Bukhari, who said: we were informed by Isma'il ibn Abi Uways, from Malik... the hadith.

There is another view regarding the verse: that it is the exposure to the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Farra' said: In the verse there is inversion and rearrangement, as if he had said: "And on the Day the Hour is established, cause the family of Pharaoh to enter the severest punishment; the Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening." This is a corrupt view, and the correct one is the first.

As for His words: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, "Cause the family of Pharaoh to enter the severest punishment."﴾ It was read: "Udkhulu Ali Fir'awn ashadda al-'adhab" (Enter, O family of Pharaoh, the severest punishment) as an imperative addressed to the family of Pharaoh to enter.

It was also read: ﴿Adkhilu Ali Fir'awn ashadda al-'adhab﴾ (Cause the family of Pharaoh to enter the severest punishment) as an imperative addressed to the keepers of the Fire.

The evidence that the first view is the correct one is that He said: ﴿They are exposed to it morning and evening﴾, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, that is entry in reality, not exposure; the exposure is in the grave, as stated in the hadith. In some exegeses it is mentioned that the disbeliever is revived in the grave every morning and evening until he sees his seat in the Fire, then Allah causes him to die a second time; so his looking at his seat in the Fire is harder for him than his death. This is an anomalous view.

As for "the family of Pharaoh," it is Pharaoh and his people. It is also said: Pharaoh himself.

The poet said:

(So do not weep for one dead after another, the beloved 'Ali and 'Abbas and the family of Abu Bakr)

Its meaning: Abu Bakr himself. It is related from 'Abd Allah ibn Awfa that he said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah with a charity which my father had sent to him, and he said: 'O Allah, bless the family of Abu Awfa.'" That is: Abu Awfa himself.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 47:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when they dispute with one another in the Fire﴾, meaning: they argue with one another in the Fire.

And His words: ﴿Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant﴾, meaning: the followers said to the leaders.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, we were to you followers﴾, meaning: followers (tabi'an, plural of tabi', "followers").

And His words: ﴿So will you relieve us of some portion of the Fire?﴾, meaning: will you bear for us some of the punishment of the Fire?

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿Those who were arrogant said: "Indeed, we are all in it."﴾ That is: the leaders and the followers, all together.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants.﴾ That is: He has separated between the servants, so He admitted the people of Paradise into Paradise, and the people of the Fire into the Fire.

And those in the Fire say to the keepers of Hell (﴿And those in the Fire say to the keepers of Hell﴾). In the narrative: they say this after they had called upon God, exalted is He, for a thousand years, and had seen no answer.

And His saying (﴿Call upon your Lord that He may lighten for us a day of the punishment﴾): that is, one single day of the days of this world.

Regarding His words, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say: "Did there not come to you your messengers with clear proofs?" They will say: "Yes." They will say: "Then call upon [your Lord]. But the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error."﴾ That is: in perdition and nullity. Its meaning is that their supplication is not answered.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 51:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers﴾. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "By clarifying the proof." Others said: "By taking retribution from their enemies." And it is related from al-Suddi, who said: "The prophets, Allah has taken charge of their victory, even if they are killed in this world, for Allah will raise up after them those who will take vengeance on their enemies for them."

And His saying: ﴿and those who believe in the life of this world﴾, meaning: and He will help those who believe in the life of this world.

And His saying: ﴿and on the day when the witnesses stand up﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection.

And "al-ashhad" (the witnesses) is the plural of "shahid" (witness), like "al-ashab" is the plural of "sahib" (companion). It is also said: "shahid" and "ashhad" like "sharif" and "ashraf."

Almost-literal translation with the required conventions:

The Exalted said: ﴿On the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: their apologies, because they have no excuse. ﴿And for them is the curse﴾, meaning: upon them is the curse. ﴿And for them is the evil abode﴾, meaning: the evil abode, which is the Fire.

Almighty God says: ﴿And We gave Moses the guidance﴾, that is, prophethood.

And His saying: ﴿and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Book﴾, that is, the Torah.
And His saying: ﴿Guidance and a reminder for people of understanding﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So be patient, indeed the promise of Allah is true, and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾. Those who permit minor sins (al-saghā'ir) upon the prophets hold on to this verse, since He commanded them to seek forgiveness for minor sins. As for those who do not permit minor sins upon the prophets, they said: He commanded seeking forgiveness as an act of worship (ta'abbud), so that by it they might attain the good pleasure of Allah, exalted is He, and so that whoever comes after them might follow their example.

And His saying: ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning﴾, that is: pray thankfully to your Lord in the evening and the morning. The evening (al-'ashi) is from the time of the sun's decline until its setting, and the morning (al-ibkar) is what lies between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 56:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah⦆ means: who repel the signs of Allah by denying them.

And His saying: ﴿without any authority having come to them⦆ means: without any proof having come to them.

And His saying: ﴿There is not in their breasts except pride⦆ means: there is nothing in their breasts except pride. The pride that is in their breasts is the arrogance of refusing to acknowledge monotheism (tawhid). It is also said: it is the seeking of dominance and supremacy over Muhammad (ﷺ).

And His saying: ﴿They will never attain it⦆ means: they will never attain what they intend. Their intention was that Muhammad (ﷺ) be destroyed, his companions be destroyed, his trace be effaced, and they become a tale. It is also said: their intention was to overcome Muhammad (ﷺ) and for their affair to prevail over his affair. There is a third opinion regarding the verse, related by Ibn Jurayj and others.

(This is that) the verse was revealed concerning the Jews. They used to say: there will emerge from among us, at the end of time, one who will prevail over the entire earth, the sea will reach his knees, the clouds will be over his head, he will kill and give life, and with him will be a mountain of paradise and a mountain of fire. They said: he means the people of knowledge, and he is the Dajjal (the Antichrist) whom the Messenger (ﷺ) mentioned. So when they said this, Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

The meaning of His saying ﴿they will never attain it⦆ according to this opinion is that dominance will not belong to the Dajjal over the Muslims; rather, dominance will belong to the Muslims over the Dajjal, for ʿIsa (peace be upon him) will descend and kill the Dajjal, in support of the Muslims.

And His saying: ﴿So seek refuge in Allah⦆ means: from the evil (shirk) of the Dajjal according to this opinion.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing⦆ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 57:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾, meaning: He raised the heavens without pillars, set the stars, the sun and the moon in their courses, spread out the earth, and planted the mountains, which is more awe-inspiring in the hearts of people than the creation of human beings. It is also said: the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than killing the Dajjal (the Antichrist) once and bringing him back to life; so "mankind" here refers, according to this view, to the Dajjal.

And His saying: ﴿But most people do not know﴾, meaning: they do not know the true reality of matters.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the blind and the one who sees are not alike﴾, up to His saying: ﴿little do you remember﴾ with the letter "ta" (تتذكرون, "you remember"), and it has also been read with the letter "ya" (يتذكرون, "they remember"). The meaning of the readings is close to one another.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, the Hour is surely coming; there is no doubt about it﴾. That is: there is no doubt concerning it.

And His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾. That is: they do not affirm it as true.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 60:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you."﴾ It is established through the narration of Nu'man ibn Bashir that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Supplication (du'a') is worship," and he recited this verse.

And from Thabit, who said: I said to Anas, "Supplication is half of worship." He said: "It is all of worship."

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disdain My worship﴾ means: those who disdain My supplication. It is also said: those who disdain My monotheism (tawhid).

And His saying: ﴿They will enter Hell in humiliation﴾ means: abased, humbled.

And from Ka'b al-Ahbar, who said: This Ummah has been given three things that no other nation has been given. God Almighty said to every prophet of the earlier ones: "You are a witness over your people," and He said to this Ummah: ﴿You are witnesses over the nations﴾. God Almighty said to every prophet: "There is no hardship upon you in the religion," and He said to this Ummah: ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾. And He said to every prophet: "Call upon Me, and I will answer you," and He said to this Ummah: ﴿Call upon Me; I will respond to you.﴾

God's words: ﴿It is Allah who made the night for you that you may rest therein﴾, i.e., that you may relax from labours therein. It is said: that you may sleep.

And His words: ﴿and the day as something to see by﴾, i.e., something in which one sees; its meaning is that people see things by it.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks﴾ — its meaning is apparent.
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no god but Him. So how are you deluded?﴾ We have already explained it.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Thus are turned away those who used to deny the signs of God.﴾ That is: whoever was a polytheist, associating others with God, and a denier of His signs, is turned away from the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 64:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the earth as a place of settlement﴾, meaning: you settle upon it, ﴿and the sky as a canopy﴾, meaning: a canopy above you.

And His saying: ﴿and He shaped you and perfected your shapes﴾. It is said in the exegesis that He does not eat with His hand anything except the children of Adam, and there is no form in this shape more beautiful than the children of Adam.

And His saying: ﴿and provided you with good things﴾, meaning: of what you find delicious, of what is lawful for you.

And His saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; so blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾. Its meaning: exalted and magnified is the Lord of the worlds above what the disbelievers say.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 65:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He is the Living; there is no god but Him, so call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His (ikhlas, sincerity of devotion)﴾. Supplication with sincerity (ikhlas) means that one does not call upon anyone else alongside Him.

And His saying: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. It is narrated from Ibn Sirin that he said: "It is from the sunnah (the prophetic normative practice) that the servant says, 'There is no god but Allah,' and then immediately after it says: 'All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'"

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah, since the clear proofs have come to me from my Lord.﴾ That is, "al-bayyinat" means the evident proofs (hujaj).

And His saying: ﴿And I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.﴾ That is, "aslama" means I surrender and yield to His judgment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 67:

The words of the Most High: ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a drop [of semen], then from a clinging clot, then He brings you forth as a child﴾. Meaning: "as children" (aṭfālan), used in the singular with the sense of the plural. It is also said: "ṭiflan ṭiflan" (one child after another).

And His words: ﴿Then that you may reach your full strength﴾. We have already explained the meaning of al-ashudd (full maturity).

And His words: ﴿Then that you may become elders, and among you is he who dies before that﴾. Meaning: before he has become an elder (shaykh).

And His words: ﴿And that you may reach an appointed term﴾. Meaning: what has been decreed for you of life.

And His words: ﴿And perhaps you will reason﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Almost-literal translation:

Allah's words, the Exalted: ﴿He is the One who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be," and it is.﴾ That is: His bringing things into being happens in a single instance, not once after another.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah?﴾ That is, they dispute about rejecting Our signs by denying them.

And His saying: ﴿How are they turned away?﴾ That is, how are they turned away from the truth?
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers—they will come to know﴾. This is a warning and a threat.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 40, verses 71–72:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When the shackles are around their necks, and the chains﴾. It is also recited as "wa-al-salasilu" (and the chains) with the lam in the accusative (wa-al-salasila). As for the one who reads it in the nominative, its meaning is: the shackles are around their necks, and the chains. As for the one who reads it in the accusative, its meaning is: and they are dragged by the chains.

And His saying: ﴿They are dragged through the boiling water﴾, meaning: they are pulled along in the boiling water.

And His saying: ﴿Then in the Fire they are kindled﴾, meaning: they are set alight in the Fire, just as ovens (tanannir, sing. tannur) are kindled with wood.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verses 73–74:

Concerning the words of the Exalted: ﴿Then it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to associate with Allah?"﴾ meaning: "Where are they, that they may help you?" And they will say, "They have vanished and gone away from us."

And His words: ﴿Nay, we used to call upon nothing before.﴾ That is: we used to call upon nothing before that could ward off harm from us or bring us benefit.

And His words: ﴿Thus Allah leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ That is: away from the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 75:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿That is because you used to exult in the land without right﴾. This is evidence that there can be exultation that is in accordance with right (ḥaqq).

And His words: ﴿and because you used to be insolent (tamrahūn)﴾. Al-farḥ (exultation) is joy (surūr). Al-marḥ, al-baṭar and al-ashr (all denote forms of arrogance and exuberance). In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) it is said that he said: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, dislikes the arrogant (al-badhkhīn), the exultant and the insolent, and He loves every grieving heart, and He dislikes the fat scholar (al-ḥibr al-samīn), and He dislikes the people of the household of the fleshy (ahl bayt al-laḥmayn)," that is, those who eat a great deal of meat. It is also said: those who eat the flesh of people through backbiting (ghība). And the report is gharīb (weak in its chain of transmission, i.e., a report transmitted through a single narrator at some stage).

Wa-qawluhu: ﴿Fadkhulū abwāba jahannam khālidīna fīhā fa-bi'sa mathwā al-mutakabbirīn﴾ — ẓāhir al-ma'nā.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿So enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein; and evil is the abode of the arrogant.﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on Surah 40, verse 77:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So be patient, for indeed the promise of Allah is true﴾, up to the end of the verse. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 78:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We certainly sent messengers before you. Among them are those whom We have related to you, and among them are those whom We have not related to you.﴾ Al-Suddi said: Allah the Exalted sent eight thousand prophets: four thousand from the Children of Israel, and four thousand from other than the Children of Israel. And in some tafsir works it is said: the total of those whom Allah the Exalted mentioned in the Qur'an among the prophets is twenty-five prophets, the first of them Adam, and the last of them Muhammad. He mentioned eighteen of them in Surat al-An'am, and the rest in other surahs. And it is reported from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that Allah the Exalted sent a prophet from Abyssinia whose name is not mentioned in the Qur'an. As for what is on the tongues of the people, that Allah the Exalted sent one hundred and twenty-four thousand prophets...

And this is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas through a weak transmission.

And His words: ﴿And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by the permission of Allah﴾. This is a reply to the disbelievers, who asked the Prophet for a specific miracle and said: "Do such-and-such." So Allah refuted that for them with His words: ﴿And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by the permission of Allah﴾.

And His words: ﴿So when the command of Allah comes, it will be decided with truth, and the falsifiers will lose there.﴾ That is: the falsifiers will be destroyed at that time.

And His words: ﴿the command of Allah﴾ He meant by it the Resurrection.

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the cattle, that you may ride some of them and eat from some of them﴾.

The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: al-an'am (cattle) are, in the language, the camels, the cows and the sheep, except that in this verse it refers specifically to the camels.

"And His saying: ﴿And for you therein are benefits﴾ meaning: besides riding and eating, from the milk (rusul), the offspring (nasl), the wool (wabr), and other things."

"And His saying: ﴿and that you may attain thereby a need in your breasts﴾. Qatadah said: the moving from one land to another. Mujahid said: whatever need it may be."

"And His saying: ﴿and upon them and upon the ship you are carried﴾. The meaning is apparent, and al-Fulk (the ship) is the boat."
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He shows you His signs, so which of Allah's signs will you deny?﴾ That is, despite their being manifest and clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 82:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not traveled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them and greater in strength and in traces left upon the earth.﴾ Mujahid said: His saying, "and traces left upon the earth," means walking upon it with their feet. It is also said: the traces upon the earth are the thrones (ʿurush, i.e., structures), the crops, and the buildings.

And His saying: ﴿So what they used to earn did not avail them.﴾ That is, their earnings did not repel anything from them when the punishment descended upon them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 83:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿When their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they exulted in the knowledge they had﴾. If it is said: how can this be consistent, when they had no knowledge at all?

We say: they thought themselves to be scholars, so He called what they had "knowledge" according to their own supposition. What they supposed was that there is no resurrection, no Garden, no Fire, and no life after death.

The second opinion regarding the verse is that His words ﴿they exulted﴾ refer to the messengers, and the meaning of the verse is: the messengers rejoiced in the knowledge they had of the destruction of their enemies.

It is also said: "they exulted in the knowledge they had" means: they were content with the knowledge they had, and did not seek the knowledge that Allah sent down to the prophets, and they settled for what they had, and that was, in truth, ignorance.

And His words ﴿And there befell them what they used to mock﴾ mean: there descended upon them the consequence of what they used to mock.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 84:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ We have already mentioned the meaning of al-ba's (the severity, or punishment).

And His saying: ﴿and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him.﴾ Thus is the case with all the disbelievers: they believe at the time of al-ba's (the moment of punishment), but that does not benefit them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 40, verse 85:

And His saying: ﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might.﴾ And a people were excepted from them, the people of Yunus, in Surat Yunus, and we have mentioned it.

And His saying: ﴿The way of Allah which has passed before among His servants.﴾ That is: it has elapsed among His servants. And the meaning of the sunnah (way/practice) is: their faith, and the non-benefit of their faith.

And His saying: ﴿And there the disbelievers were lost.﴾ That is: there the disbelievers perished.

If it is said: how did He say ﴿there﴾ (hunalika), when this requires that they were not in the state of being lost?

The answer: al-Zajjaj said: every disbeliever is lost, except that when he sees the punishment, his loss becomes manifest to him. It is in this sense that He said ﴿there﴾, and Allah knows best.
